title: 樫本代理の意外な一面

text_block_list.text: One day, as I'm carrying a huge stack of books to help with our training…
A strong gust of wind knocks me off balance, and the books hit the ground with a pronounced thud.

text_block_list.name: Riko Kashimoto
text_block_list.text: Hmph… That was an unsightly blunder.

text_block_list.name: Riko Kashimoto
text_block_list.text: You should've bundled the books together—or better yet, not tried to carry so many in the first place. Your risk management is lacking.

text_block_list.name: Riko Kashimoto
text_block_list.text: It's fortunate no students were around. What would you have done if you injured someone?
I hurriedly crouch down to pick up the books, and to my surprise, Ms. Kashimoto starts helping too.

text_block_list.name: Riko Kashimoto
text_block_list.text: There's no need to look that shocked.

text_block_list.name: Riko Kashimoto
text_block_list.text: Many hands make light work. Now hurry. There are still more over there.
Ms. Kashimoto swiftly picks up the remaining books and hands them to me.

text_block_list.name: Riko Kashimoto
text_block_list.text: Just so you know, there's a glaring spelling error in one of your page markers—adverse conditions "affect" a student's running, not "effect."

text_block_list.name: Riko Kashimoto
text_block_list.text: You're one of the most trusted adults in your students' lives. Do better to set a good example.
Ms. Kashimoto walks off, seemingly unfazed.
She gives off a cold and detached impression, but could she be surprisingly kind underneath it all?
Thanks to her help, I manage to transport all the books intact, and I use them to formulate some improved training plans.
